AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Livestock Products? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Livestock Products.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Livestock Products.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Products.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Livestock Products.

3. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agroforestry? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agroforestry.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Agroforestry.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agroforestry.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agroforestry.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Pest control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Pest control.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Pest control.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Pest control.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Pest control.

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Aquaculture.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Aquaculture.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Aquaculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Aquaculture.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water conservation.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water conservation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water conservation.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water conservation.

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Parasite control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Parasite control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Parasite control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Parasite control.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Parasite control.

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Inorganic fertilisers? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Inorganic fertilisers.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Inorganic fertilisers.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Inorganic fertilisers.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Inorganic fertilisers.

13. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

14. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Rearing Selected Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Rearing Selected Animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Rearing Selected Animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Rearing Selected Animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Rearing Selected Animals.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Digestive systems of animals? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Digestive systems of animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Digestive systems of animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Digestive systems of animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Digestive systems of animals.

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Production Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Production Structures.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Production Structures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Production Structures.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Production Structures.

18. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Vegetative propagation? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Vegetative propagation.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Vegetative propagation.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Vegetative propagation.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Vegetative propagation.

20. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

21. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

22. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structures in Animal production? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Structures in Animal production.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structures in Animal production.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structures in Animal production.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structures in Animal production.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
23. In three clear sentences, explain Agroforestry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Protection: Pest control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Production Structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Digestive systems of animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Parasite control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Structures in Animal production and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Aquaculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Rearing Selected Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

31. In three clear sentences, explain Livestock Products and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

32. In three clear sentences, explain Powered Tools and Equipment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
